articleTitle: The nexus between design and control: a data-driven approach for leveraging flexibility potential of micro-grids
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This research focuses on optimizing energy efficiency and flexibility in institutional and residential buildings within an energy community/micro-grid in Varennes, Québec. Employing data-driven building models, the paper proposes an energy modelling methodology utilising resistance-capacitance (RC) thermal networks to predict the building thermal loads. Electrical base loads are instead evaluated through regression and clustering techniques. The study incorporates on-site solar energy production and communal batteries to comprehensively analyse their impact on the whole energy consumption. The objective is the optimization of thermal and electrical management at both local and communal levels. This is assessed by employing a double-stage model predictive control (MPC) routine, also providing insights on the nexus between design and operation. Emphasizing day-ahead flexibility, the effects of various events on resiliency are assessed. Based on a preliminary energy assessment for the specific period of study, a photovoltaic system ranging from 150 to 200 kWp and a battery storage system ranging from 100 to 200 kWh are recommended for a community made of one house and one institutional building. These systems will ensure efficient energy supply and management, promoting sustainability and reducing reliance on traditional grid sources by over 20%.

articleTitle: The Study of Urban Heat Island Effect in Limassol, Cyprus Using Sentinel-3 Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The Heat Island Effect causes discomfort for residents in the affected areas and has a negative impact on the environment, increasing the effects of climate change and placing more people at risk. The most widely used approach for detecting and studying the Heat Island Effect through remote sensing is by utilizing thermal satellite imagery of the surface at night.In this study, the Copernicus Sentinel-3 satellite's Land-surface temperature (LST) products were used to extract surface temperature from night images and generate heat maps of Limassol, Cyprus. The study looked at time-series data for the hottest day in the month of July, during the period of 2017 to 2024. Such information is critical to understand the areas affected by the Heat Island Effect and to support decision-makers and policymakers in developing effective mitigation strategies to enhance urban planning.

articleTitle: Power quality analysis of railway traction power substation using eighteen-pulse rectifier phase-shifting transformer system
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Electrified railways are powered by dedicated traction power substations (TPSSs) that represent nonlinear loads for the utility supply network. Power Quality (PQ) problems affect both the three-phase network that feeds the TPSS and the contact line, which completes the traction system. The goal of this study was to evaluate the harmonics generated by an 18 pulse AC/DC rectifier for railway traction, and to compare the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) between 6-pulse, 12-pulse, and 18-pulse conversion stations. Moreover, a new configuration of the 18-pulse conversion system is proposed, and the effects of low-voltage (LV) active filtering are reported. Starting from a MATLAB-Simulink model of the TPSS of 6 and 12 pulses, a software simulation of the 18-pulse rectifier was performed. Then, by using the software tool FFT Analyzer, a charter was generated showing the values of the harmonics at specific frequencies and the evaluation of the THD. The current and voltage harmonics introduced by rectifiers in the threephase power line providing power supply to the TPSS were evaluated. The 18-pulse configuration improved the THD on the currents by approximately 20% with respect to the 12-pulse configuration. The last part of the paper focuses on the new architecture proposed in this paper by connecting active filters in parallel to each converter to further improve PQ by 40%, allowing the revamping of existing substations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Efficiency and Sustainability with Hybrid AC/DC Microgrids for Energy Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The transition to a lower-carbon energy system across Europe brings numerous opportunities and challenges, necessitating advancements in sustainable and eco-friendly energy solutions. This study examines the design and operation of distribution networks and microgrids, particularly emphasizing the integration of hybrid AC/DC distribution systems. The primary goals of this integration are to enhance overall system performance and reduce operating expenses. Utilizing DIgSILENT Power Factory software, the research simulates a microgrid at the FOSS Research Center for Sustainable Energy at the University of Cyprus, incorporating real load and PV generation data. In order to reduce the amount of energy imported from the main grid, this approach evaluates various combinations of AC and DC loads, power production units, and energy storage solutions. The results show that the most optimal structure, with 65% DC loads and 35% AC loads, maximizes efficiency as well as minimizes running expenses. The analysis highlights a notable decrease in imported energy, which dropped from 60.3 kWh/day at full AC loads to 51.6 kWh/day at the optimal DC ratio. Finally, the design and implementation of effective, sustainable energy systems that are in line with changing European energy policy and technology breakthroughs will be significantly impacted by these outcomes.

articleTitle: George Kelly’s repertory grid as a tool for probing entrepreneurial cognition for sustainable innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This article describes, contextualises and justifies an approach to the evaluation of entrepreneurship and innovation training and culture development to be applied in the EU Teaming project Phaethon, drawing on our previous work on this topic. We first explain that research of entrepreneurship involving sustainability norms, as well as the other criteria that new products and services need to fulfil, is still relatively new, and that study of education and training in this area is even more recent and limited. We provide a brief overview of both. We then explain our proposed method of investigation, which is the use of interviews involving George Kelly’s repertory grids. This is a social constructivist form of question design in which the terms of the questions are based on interviews with participants, with the aim being to understand the terms in which participants experience and perceive particular aspects of the world.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of solar-driven PEM water electrolysis systems for hydrogen production
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: With the increasing demand for promoting the utilisation of renewable and clean energy resources, solar-driven proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis systems have gained significant attention as an effective energy conversion technology for green hydrogen production. This study aims to address the performance difference among different configurations of solar-driven PEM water electrolysis systems, so as to provide guidance for system design and optimisation. By coupling TRNSYS with MATLAB, we have established a model for annual performance simulation, based on which comparative analysis of photovoltaic-PEM (PV-PEM), PV/thermal-PEM (PV/T-PEM), and PV-solar thermal-PEM (PV-ST-PEM) systems has been performed, using meteorological data from Nicosia, the capital of the Republic of Cyprus. The results demonstrate that the PV/T-PEM system achieves the highest average solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 3.5% and PEM energy efficiency of 80.0 % on a typical day in summer. The PV/T-PEM system also exhibit annual hydrogen production of 57.1 L/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. By employing PV/T collectors, electricity and thermal energy can be simultaneously generated without compromising the solar array area dedicated to electricity generation compared to the PV-ST configuration. It can be concluded that PV/T-PEM systems hold significant potential as a viable solution for enhancing energy efficiency for hydrogen generation.

articleTitle: Ameliorated quantum class topper optimization to solve economic load dispatch problems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This article proposes an ameliorated quantum class topper optimization (A-QCTO) to address the economic load dispatch (ELD) optimization problem in power systems. The A-QCTO emulates the learning behavior of students by employing a quantum mechanism and uses the cooperative escalation coefficient and dynamic improvement factor to enhance the exploration and exploitation abilities for faster and more efficient solutions to non-linear ELD problems. To validate the usefulness and robustness of the proposed algorithm, it is applied to two different test systems, i.e., ELD with valve point loading effect and cubic function ELD problems. Simulation outcomes of the test system are compared with well-known previously developed algorithms. The results show superiority in obtaining optimal fuel cost with a high convergence rate. The analysis shows its capability to handle different non-linear problems and efficiently distribute the generation with lower operation fuel costs, facilitating the electric distribution utilities and power system operators. Therefore, the proposed A-QCTO algorithm is a promising approach for solving non-linear ELD problems with higher convergence and desirable practical solutions.

articleTitle: Considering Li-Ion Battery Cell Ageing in Energy Storage Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Lithium Ion (Li-ion) cells are strong choices for energy storage within grid systems, balancing renewable supply and demand. Li-ion cells can have high durability and long lifetimes. They offer high durability and long lifespans but experience complex electrochemical and mechanical degradation that affects performance and control calibration. Key ageing mechanisms include electrode surface layer formation, lithium deposition, electrolyte deterioration, and damage to electrodes and current collectors. These mechanisms depend on electrode chemistry and usage conditions. It is essential to consider them when designing battery packs, selecting cell chemistry, and planning thermal management. The complex non-linear changes in cell behaviour must also be considered during usage. Control systems must account for complex, condition-based changes in cell behaviour, requiring sophisticated modelling and analysis of ageing effects to optimize the trade-off between usage and depreciation. This paper explains Li-ion cell ageing and its consequences in the context of stationary storage applications.

articleTitle: Development of Distribution-level Multi-domain Synchronized Measurements for FNET/GridEye
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth review of the evolution of distribution-level monitoring sensors used in the FNET/GridEye system. It details the technological advancements and the impact of three generations of sensors on grid monitoring. It highlights significant improvements in precision, sampling rates, and real-time data processing, contributing to enhanced grid stability and reliability.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation Improved by Stochastic Disturbance Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the functional integration of a load compensation logic into the secondary voltage regulation strategy. The objective is to integrate FACTS devices into the control strategy for compensating for fast variations of load power while controlling the generators in the traditional way, as if the load variations were zero. The generators are controlled according to an optimal linear quadratic control logic, while FACTS devices provide compensating reactive power based on the estimate of load variations. PMUs data are used to model the fast load variations as a multivariate stochastic process of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck type. The estimation of this multivariate process is carried out using a Bayesian methodology, easily done and characterized by excellent accuracy. In the final part of the paper, the implementation procedure of the regulation logic is exposed. The numerical results obtained allow us to confirm the validity of the proposed regulation strategy.

articleTitle: Operational strategies for a photovoltaic-thermal system integrated with an electric air-to-water heat pump
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: In this study, operational strategies are investigated for an air-based photovoltaic-thermal (PV-T) system integrated with a domestic air-to-water heat pump. The PV-T system is used to simultaneously generate electricity and heat ambient air, which serves as the heat source for the heat pump. By utilising a variable-speed fan to regulate airflow, the PV-T system outlet temperature is adjusted, and the focus is on how different outlet temperatures impact the PVT system electrical and thermal efficiency, heat pump performance, and overall electricity requirements for heating. The performance of the integrated system is assessed for a case study of a household application in north Italy. The optimal PV-T outlet temperature is found to be between 30 – 35 °C, resulting in only 5% less electricity production than an equivalent PV system with equal nominal electricity capacity, while reducing overall electricity required for heating by over 15% compared to PV-integrated heat pumps.

articleTitle: Increasing Wind Power Harvest while Minimizing Power System Disturbances Using a Modified Wind Turbine Generation Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Power system operation under varying generations and demands is challenging, and integration of intermittent wind power complicates the system even more. Wind power generation under heavy winds is associated with power fall-outs from the power system due to the wind speeds exceeding the maximum limits of the turbine. These sudden power withdrawals at high wind speeds could be associated with some economic losses due to untapped energy concentration available at such speeds. This is in addition to power system disturbances that are likely to occur in a hybrid system operation, which, if not properly tackled can cause other serious system issues and even collapse depending on the magnitude of the injected power from the wind farm. Using excessive spinning reserves as is sometimes done to deal with the resulting fall-outs may not be a suitable option, considering the heavy economic implications of running the reserves. A solution to this issue is proffered in this work by using an innovative method. A wind turbine with a modified power characteristics curve is proposed, such that the turbine continues to operate with reduced output power beyond the normal cut-off point instead of a total sudden generation withdrawal. The results obtained in this method have indicated power system stability enhancement in addition to improvement in power harvests. A multi-period dispatch operation with wind will greatly benefit from this.

articleTitle: Sizing and operation of hybrid photovoltaic – battery energy storage system in islanded power networks with high renewable energy curtailments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Power networks are currently challenged by high renewable energy curtailments (REC), a countereffect of renewables’ sporadic nature and high photovoltaic (PV) penetration in grids. This work aims to provide sizing and operation insights for battery energy storage systems (BESS) coupled with PVs, as a solution to mitigate REC, especially in islanded power networks. The derived REC analysis and simulation model results demonstrated the attractiveness of longer BESS-duration and quantified the examined asset’s environmental and financial impact. Notably, the longer BESS-duration managed to utilise the available (curtailed) energy to the greatest extent and extended time utilisation. The obtained results provided insights for the practicality of BESS power and energy capacity, useful to policymakers, system operators, and investors for avoiding unnecessary or ineffective investments.

articleTitle: Next-Day Solar Irradiance Forecasting: A Preliminary Study in Limassol
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This study presents a preliminary evaluation of a next-day solar irradiance forecast system in Limassol, Cyprus, over six months. For the evaluation, forecasted Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) was compared with high-quality ground measurements. The system showed strong correlation with measured values at both hourly and daily timescales. Hourly forecasts exhibited a correlation coefficient (r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) of 0.84 and a Mean Bias Error (MBE) of 23.4 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (4.8%), while daily energy forecasts showed improved performance with an r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.86 and an MBE of 0.3 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (4.7%). The Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) was 123.7 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (25.4%) for hourly forecasts and 0.8 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (13%) for daily forecasts, indicating that daily aggregation reduces error magnitudes by averaging out short-term fluctuations and discrepancies. Some discrepancies were due to the model’s limited ability to capture cloud and aerosol variations. Future work will focus on investigating these factors to enhance the forecast system’s accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Use of a Hybrid Storage System for Frequency Regulation Services from a Photovoltaic Plant: Emulating Synchronous Generator Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The gradual decommissioning of grid-forming synchronous generators and the increasing penetration of grid-following renewable energy sources such as photovoltaics (PVs), undermine the reliable operation of the grid. In this sense, even small power imbalances can cause significant frequency deviations. To address such issues, the employment of standalone battery storage systems is usually proposed to alleviate the power imbalances by releasing/absorbing energy when needed. However, a standalone battery suffers from quick lifetime fading and it cannot effectively provide multiple grid services simultaneously. To this end, this study presents a controller for a hybrid storage system that consists of a power-type superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) and an energy-type battery. The hybrid storage system is AC-coupled and provides frequency regulation services on behalf of the PV plant without any modification on its inverter. Through proper control, SMES handles the short-term power fluctuations emulating the inertial properties of a synchronous generator, while battery cope with long-term demands imitating the primary frequency response of the generator. Thus, the distinct features of both SMES and battery are effectively exploited, ensuring minimal stress on battery. To evaluate the proposed method during grid frequency events, simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Smart control of a public building nanogrid: the Italian pilot of the BERLIN project
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The Energy Management System plays a key role in nanogrid implementation. Indeed, suitably coordinating the operation of the available energy resources allows for improving the energy performance of the nanogrid, for instance, maximising its self-consumption. The paper describes the test case of the pilot plant installed in one University of Cagliari campus building for the European BERLIN project. The developed algorithm optimises the charging and discharging phases of a Battery Energy Storage System based on the actual measurements and the foreseen estimations of the photovoltaic production and the building electricity consumption. Additional input, such as weather conditions or electricity signal price, can be considered. The tool was initially developed and tested offline using an RTDS simulator in a Software-in-the-Loop configuration and finally uploaded to the Energy Management System for real-time operation. The simulated results show the potential benefits of an optimised operation, the importance of the correct sizing of the nanogrid energy resources and the dependency on the electricity consumption profile. Indeed, the specific features of the pilot site reveal that if the equipment sizing is not optimally tailored and load shaping margins are limited, it could be equivalent to adopting simple battery management logic.

articleTitle: Innovation Management in Research Infrastructure Services for Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: To achieve more efficient, competitive and cost-effective energy systems and devices, the project RISEnergy (Research Infrastructure Services for Renewable Energy) wants to create an ecosystem of industry in Europe, research organizations and funding agencies. That aims to develop novel energy technologies and concepts. The project is consisted of a consortium of 69 beneficiaries from 23 countries: vocational education and training institutes, technology institutes, universities and industrial partners, to jointly improve the economic performance of technologies. The purpose is to enable research and innovation to increase energy efficiency and reduce the cost of energy technologies, to foster wider use of renewables into energy systems through proactive innovation management having one entry point to Research Infrastructure providers. We present the inclusion for the first time of Innovation Management in a research infrastructure (RI) services project. The reported work aims to provide support and guidance to technology developers after the product/service has been tested to reach commercial potential and create technological advancements of new technologies, solutions and systems. To maximize the benefit regarding knowledge sharing, improving processes and streamlining to help and de-risk innovative technologies prior to commercialisation. In this paper the planned work to be performed and the expected outcomes of the Innovation Management team will be presented. The aim is to demonstrate the importance of Innovation in RI projects and generate a constantly growing repository of best practices from lessons learnt.

articleTitle: A modified Five-Level NPC Transformer-less Bi-directional Solar Home Converter for Grid Services
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The increasing demand for renewable energy has driven significant advancements in power conversion technologies, particularly single-phase inverters, vital for solar integrated dwellings. Despite the benefits of single-phase inverters, including transformer-less designs and multilevel topologies, several challenges remain, such as managing high ground currents, providing frequency and reactive power support to the grid and ensuring low-cost, high-efficiency solutions. This paper explores the evolving landscape of inverter technology, highlighting innovations in transformer-less and modified multilevel converter operations. A strong emphasis is placed on the necessity for advanced bi-directional inverters that can offer grid services. The paper presents a novel operating principle for a T-Type 5-level neutral point-clamped inverter that functions in both inverter and rectifier modes. This design adheres to grid codes EN 50438 and EN 50549 using traditional dq control methods. The MATLAB-based simulation platform is used to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Power Hardware-in-the-Loop Testing of a Data-Driven Multi-Ancillary Services Framework Provided by Photovoltaic/Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The scope of this paper is to test a multi-ancillary services architecture provided by distributed photovoltaic-battery storage systems with power hardware-in-the-loop (PHiL) experimental validation. The examined ancillary services are provided to overcome voltage violation and voltage unbalance issues. A distinct feature of the proposed solution is the efficient decoupling between the voltage regulation and the voltage unbalance mitigation control schemes. The PHiL study reflects a small distribution network test case and offers a good insight and evaluation of the proposed ancillary services architecture.

articleTitle: Comparison of Fast Frequency Response Methods in the Low-Inertia Grid of Cyprus
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Modern electric power systems with high levels of penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) often present frequency security problems. The lack of inertia due to the reduced number of synchronous generators in these systems, in combination with the usual inability of RES to provide frequency support, leads to system operators having to curtail RES or rely heavily on Under Frequency Load Shedding schemes to ensure frequency security. Fast Frequency Reserves (FFR) have been proposed as a solution to strengthen the frequency support of the system and alleviate security problems. FFR allows mitigating Rate of Change of Frequency, Nadir, and post-fault frequency steady-state problems after an event. In this paper, we present, analyze, implement and compare five FFR controllers to alleviate frequency security problems in low-inertia grids. The low-inertia, islanded, Cyprus dynamic model is used to quantify the results and exhibit the impact on a real system.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of an Anion Exchange Membrane Electrolyzer for Integration in a Novel Solar Photovoltaic-Battery-Green Hydrogen Nanogrid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The Mediterranean area is an ideal location for harnessing solar energy due to the high solar irradiation availability. Utilization of innovative solutions address renewable energy instabilities and optimize the utilization of local clean energy resources. A promising technology is the utilization of green hydrogen subsystem to these solar systems. Such an integration could add significant capabilities, namely, provision of seasonal energy storage, increase of solar photovoltaic capacity, and export of the generated green hydrogen for other uses, such as fueling of hydrogen electric vehicles. A detailed model is developed in this work to assess the performance of the proposed green hydrogen subsystem configuration with a view to utilizing it as part of a future, larger, wholistic energy system. At full-load the model performs at an efficiency of 62.4%, while performance at a 10% part-load is 82.3%. These performance results suggest a very promising potential for this technology which can be harnessed in the future multi-scale energy systems, provided that the economic performance is also promising.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Security Assessment Tool for Modern Power Systems with Massive RES Penetration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Modern power systems are facing significant challenges due to the massive penetration of renewable energy sources (RES). Recently, issues related to frequency security, system strength, and excessive fault levels have been experienced in some power systems. Classical dynamic security assessment (DSA) tools have not been developed to identify and analyze these new challenges that are critical in low-inertia grids. In this paper, a DSA tool has been developed that evaluates frequency security, system strength, and maximum fault levels to allow for secure system planning and operation. Furthermore, to increase the accuracy of the DSA tool, inverter-based resources’ (IBRs’) protections and capabilities have been incorporated in the DSA tool. A real-time operation and an operational planning application of the DSA tool are showcased using the islanded Cyprus Power System.

articleTitle: Enhancing Management and Control of Renewable Energy Communities: A Practical Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Renewable Energy Communities are integral to the European Commission's energy transition agenda. These communities foster the participation of citizens, local authorities, and enterprises in producing, exchanging, and consuming renewable energy locally. The community members benefit from various financial incentives, including payments for excess renewable production, a premium tariff for renewable shared energy, and the refund of part of the electricity bill. However, high penetration of renewable energy sources can challenge grid stability, necessitating the adoption of flexibility strategies like battery systems and demand-side management. This paper presents a prototype of a tool for the real-time optimal management of renewable energy communities in which renewable generation, electrical loads and batteries are present. The community management tool implements: algorithms for forecasting load consumption and renewable generation; and algorithms for the optimal management of controllable resources.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Proton Exchange Membrane Electrolyzer-Compressed Hydrogen Storage-Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Green Hydrogen Subsystem for Integration to a Solar Photovoltaic-Battery Nanogrid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: A Photovoltaic-Battery-Green Hydrogen nanogrid system is designed and modeled to investigate its potential as a decentralized energy solution able to satisfy the load profile of Near Zero Energy Buildings. Such a system could potentially maximize self-consumption through onsite power generation, which also achieves minimization of dependence on the central power grid. The proposed system includes battery and hydrogen energy storage for various purposes. Such a combination could succeed in satisfying both the need for rapid power supply when needed (through battery energy storage), but it can also provide seasonal energy storage when the weather pattern of available solar energy changes between summer and winter (through hydrogen energy storage). The Green Hydrogen subsystem includes electrolyzer and fuel cell units, both based on proton exchange membrane technology, a hydrogen storage unit, and auxiliary components. The proposed system generates 110 kg of hydrogen per year, with electrolyzer and fuel cell efficiencies (at full load design conditions) at 58.4% and 45.8%, respectively. Self-sufficiency rate is close to 100%, while self-consumption rate is slightly below 48%.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Building Energy Flexibility Using Monitored Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper presents a framework for assessing building energy flexibility using measured data. A Canadian residential building with onsite solar power system is used to demonstrate the methodology. Five energy flexibility metrics are evaluated: self-generation, self-consumption, loss of load probability (LOLP), energy autonomy, and building energy flexibility index (BEFI). The results show that the building generates 43.2% of its energy demand and consumes 43.7% of its PV supply. The LOLP and energy autonomy metrics reveal that the local power supply meets the building’s total demand 40% of the time. Additionally, the building shows a BEFI of 16.4%, and a power density of 12.4 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, indicating its average power flexibility during demand response events. The framework assesses the performance of grid-interactive buildings and provides useful insights for decision-making on effective flexibility strategies. It can be adapted to different building archetypes and is a fundamental preparatory process in developing control-oriented datasets.

articleTitle: Droop-Control-Aided State Estimation in Active Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced state estimation algorithm for active distribution systems (DSs) is presented. Its distinct characteristic is the integration of the local control logic of the distributed renewable energy sources, i.e., the droop control, into the mathematical formulation of the state estimation problem. Numerical results on a real medium-voltage DS are presented to highlight the superior performance of the proposed method against the conventional weighted least squares estimation algorithm in terms of increased accuracy and observability.

articleTitle: Optimizing Building Performance: A Novel Digital Twin Framework for Enhanced Thermal Comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology has evolved from a theoretical concept to a practical tool with widespread applications. In the built environment, DT serves as a virtual representation of physical buildings, integrating data from sensors, Building Information Modeling (BIM), and historical performance to monitor, analyze, and optimize building operations. Despite extensive research in this field, gaps remain, particularly in providing quantitative results and integrating DT frameworks with building control systems. Addressing these gaps, this study proposes a novel DT framework designed to optimize building performance. Utilizing BIM, data visualization tools, and a custom Building Energy Model (BEM), the framework offers real-time feedback to control systems, tested in a virtual environment (Simulation In the Loop – SIL) to demonstrate its benefits, particularly in optimizing thermal comfort by providing energy consumption insights. Quantitative analyses highlight the potential of DT technology in enhancing building performance.

articleTitle: Towards Detecting Non-Technical Losses in Electrical Power Systems with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: In this paper, Machine Learning (ML) techniques are applied to address the critical challenges of non-technical losses (NTLs) in electrical power systems. The NTL study focuses on a comprehensive dataset obtained from the Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO) in Greece, mainly collected from traditional metering systems. A careful preprocessing and feature engineering framework is implemented to prepare the (imbalanced) data for ML analysis. Several ML models are examined including Multinomial Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest and advanced ensemble techniques like XGBoost and CatBoost. The obtained results demonstrate that ensemble models, particularly CatBoost, perform best in detecting NTLs, showing high effectiveness in differentiating between normal and fraudulent consumption patterns, leading to improved detection and prevention of NTLs in power distribution networks.

articleTitle: Characterization of Voltage Fluctuations: A Methodology to KPI Analysis and Anomaly Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This work presents an algorithm designed to analyse voltage signals in Photovoltaic (PV) systems that aim to describe voltage changes in terms of operation and maintenance (O&M) corrective actions for further PV yield optimization. The algorithm examines daily voltage Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to detect and diagnose abnormalities. The process employs stringent data quality checks, statistical analysis, and control charts. The results clearly indicate the effectiveness of the system in identifying performance impairing issues, such as fluctuations in voltage, obstruction of sunlight by vegetation, accumulation of dirt, and decreases in voltage levels. Visual evaluation emphasises the significance of these diagnostics for proactive maintenance, and thereby guaranteeing the reliability and effectiveness of PV systems. This methodology improves the operating performance of PV systems, hence enhancing their sustainability and economic feasibility.

articleTitle: Bayesian Neural Networks for Direct Short-Term Net Load Forecasting in Solar-Integrated Residential Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Short-term net load forecasting (STNLF) is of utmost importance for the efficient operation and control of residential buildings, with integrated photovoltaic (PV) systems. The intermittent PV generation increases the uncertainty of STNLF and therefore the error. This study presents a machine learning model using Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) for direct STNLF in solar-integrated residential buildings. Historical data from PV-integrated households in Cyprus, with self-sufficiency between 88.59% and 294.12%, were used for assessing the performance of the BNN model. The proposed model was applied to data from 68 individual and aggregated households in Cyprus. The results indicated that the machine learning model exhibited normalized root mean square error of 7.20% for the aggregated data, rendering it suitable for STNLF in residential buildings. Finally, the model was compared to a naïve persistence model, achieving a skill score of 46.37% at the aggregated household level.

articleTitle: Predicting Energy Market Imbalance Prices with Random Forest: A Rolling Window Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Balancing supply and demand is essential for electricity grid stability, particularly with the increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RES). Accurate forecasting of imbalance prices can significantly enhance grid management and market efficiency. This study focuses on predicting imbalance prices in the Finnish market using a rolling window approach with a Random Forest (RF) model, addressing the variable nature of renewable energy sources (RES). The RF model demonstrated high forecasting accuracy across three cross-validation periods, achieving a highest coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.906 and a normalized root mean squared error (nRMSE) of 2.874% in the first period. When applied to the test set, the model yielded an R² of 0.90 and an nRMSE of 4.29%, effectively capturing non-linear and complex behaviors in imbalance prices. These results indicate that the RF model is a robust tool for imbalance price prediction, aiding market participants and system operators in enhancing decision-making and planning. Future research could explore the model's application in other markets and under various price conditions.

articleTitle: Data-driven Predictive Maintenance Alerting Routine for utility-scale Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Predictive maintenance is crucial for optimizing the performance of photovoltaic (PV) systems by proactively addressing potential issues before they escalate. Even though many fault diagnosis methods have been proposed, a major challenge remains the lack of accurate predictive maintenance routines for utility-scale PV systems. The scope of this work is to address this fundamental challenge by proposing a data-driven predictive maintenance alerting routine (that leverages digital twin technologies and decision rules) for detecting and predicting PV system faults. The results demonstrated that the developed predictive maintenance routine yielded a sensitivity of 93.9% for PV utility-scale failure detection over a yearly test period. The findings of the predictive maintenance alerting model proved its capability to anticipate faults up to 10 days in advance, achieving a sensitivity of 83.3%. Finally, the predictive maintenance alerting system can be used by operation and maintenance teams for scheduling corrective actions and optimizing field activities.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification Methodology for Photovoltaic Systems Through AI-based Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper presents a Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) methodology using an Artificial Intelligence-based (AI-based) Digital Twin (DT). Initially, the AI-based DT simulates the generated photovoltaic (PV) power under specific environmental conditions. Subsequently, the FDC methodology assesses the system state and classifies faults. The case study in the paper considers four types of faults (shading, open circuit in one string, open circuit in two strings, and open circuit in three strings). Additionally, the time series of PV power production used in this study were simulated using MATLAB Simulink, considering real meteorological conditions with a recording frequency of one hour. The simplicity of the proposed methodology ensures its applicability to large-scale PV systems, with results indicating up to 93.6% fault classification accuracy and 100% fault detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Systematic Design Approach Towards Optimizing Agri-PV Systems in Tree Crops: The Case of SolarHub
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Environmental considerations necessitate the use of Photovoltaics (PV) for electricity generation by end users. One limiting factor towards rapid expansion of this technology is the fact that PVs often take up space that is useful in the primary sector (agriculture). In this context, solutions promoting the combined use of farming and PV generation have been proposed. These solutions are often referred to as agri-PVs. As an emerging approach, agri-PVs require a more systematic analysis and deployment framework. Depending on the crop type, one could possibly optimize the design in order to improve the local crop conditions (microclimate), exploit previously untapped resources and still achieve a substantial amount of local and environmentally friendly electricity generation, to cope with climate change. In line with this, the EU project SolaHub attempts to define a relevant framework for optimizing the yield of a variety of crops such as vines and peach trees.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Condition Monitoring Scheme For Photovoltaic Systems using Programmable Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Environmental and other stresses are constantly affecting photovoltaic (PV) components which can end in various faults. The anomalous condition can reduce the PV output power or even result in a calamitous fire hazard. Hence, PV systems must be monitored constantly in order to ensure their proper performance. This paper proposes an intelligent PV condition monitoring scheme based on Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). This scheme monitors the PV performance and detects different faults and failures on the DC-side of the array. It also takes advantage of Human-Machine Interface (HMI) which provides the operators with useful real-time data from the array.

articleTitle: Design and testing of a DC Power Electronics Assembly for Experiments involving SMES and Hybrid Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage (SMES) systems offer efficient storage of electrical energy through the use of superconducting coils. However, practical experimentation with SMES systems is limited due to the complexity and cost associated with their development and operation. This paper presents the design and construction of a laboratory power electronics assembly aimed at performing small-scale SMES system tests. The assembly integrates components for linking SMES systems, batteries, loads, and sources like photovoltaic (PV) simulators to a common DC bus. Key components include half-bridge and full-bridge DC choppers, a battery energy storage system (BESS) controller and a DC load controller. The design methodology, construction procedures and cooling simulations are discussed in detail. Experimental testing of the assembly demonstrates its effectiveness in charging, idling, and discharging of the SMES system. Overall, this study contributes to advancing practical experimentation with SMES systems, offering insights into construction methodologies and experimental outcomes.

articleTitle: Characterization and Degradation of perovskite mini-modules
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: A holistic approach was utilized in this work to characterize perovskite mini-modules. Outdoor testing in combination with advanced optoelectronic techniques (spatially resolved Electroluminescence/Photoluminescence) were applied for the testing of the devices. In this way, investigation of the power output evolution of the devices in the field as well as study of their defects and shunts evolution will be performed. A considerable reduction of the power output was obtained from the devices exposed outdoors from the first days of testing. Moreover, reference modules of the same structure were kept indoors in dark storage and measured regularly with means of IV and spatially-resolved EL/PL for the study of their performance degradation under dark and controlled conditions indoors.

articleTitle: Mobility for future V2G mass deployment scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: V2G (Vehicle to Grid) is a concept that aims to utilize the capacity of vehicle batteries when vehicles (primarily cars) are stationary. It effectively gives rise to a bi-directional flow of energy between vehicles and the "grid" and "sees" them either as "storage" or as a (virtual) source of energy in order to provide services related to e.g. ancillary services-frequency regulation. Such a concept aims to make better use of network resources and provide a homogeneous flow and utilization of energy among stakeholders e.g. producers, consumers etc. In this paper we will sketch a future scenario of a mass deployment of V2G-enabled vehicles and investigate on a system-level basis the "mobility" dimension present in mobile communication networks.

articleTitle: Operational Digital Twinning: A Pathway to Flexible Building Autonomy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Digital twins have emerged as a transformative technology, enabling precise design and efficient project management in the built environment during the planning and construction phases. As buildings transition into their operational phase, the nature of collected information changes and the scope of digital twins evolves significantly, shifting towards real-time adaptive decision-making centered on continuous system performance monitoring. This paper introduces the concept of the Operational Digital Twin (ODT), a virtual counterpart to the built environment that emphasizes operational aspects, integrates real-time indoor condition monitoring, stores historical data, and simulates short-term responses to various strategies. By facilitating near-optimal decisions, ODTs enhance energy flexibility and user experience. The paper explores key applications, opportunities, and challenges associated with operational digital twins, providing a comprehensive framework for their implementation and impact.

articleTitle: Power Oscillations Damping Controller for a M-SSSC FACTS Device: the SmartValve™ case
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: To meet the evolving demands of the transmission system, it is crucial to augment its transport capacity. However, financial limitations often make the expansion of power systems unfeasible. Instead, leveraging Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) can effectively increase capacity while providing essential flexibility to the system. Beyond their core function of controlling power flow, FACTS can also be employed to reduce power oscillations. This paper investigates the integration of a Power Oscillation Damping (POD) controller within a modular Static Synchronous Series Compensator (M-SSSC). The main goal of this controller is to rapidly decrease the amplitude and settling time of inter-area oscillations, thereby improving system stability. Time-domain simulations performed using the PSCAD software confirm the controller’s effectiveness in damping inter-area oscillations. The findings indicate that integrating a POD controller into an M-SSSC significantly mitigates oscillations and maintains low peak values.

articleTitle: Grid-Forming PV System for Frequency Ancillary Services Provision
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems posing challenges to power system stability, this paper investigates the effectiveness of grid-forming controlled PV systems in providing frequency ancillary services. The study implements the Virtual Synchronous Machine strategy, utilizing DC-link capacitor energy for inertial response provision (DCVQVSM), integrated within a grid-forming topology. To ensure power-frequency droop control, an additional control loop is introduced within the DCVQ-VSM topology. The efficacy of this control system is proved through simulations conducted on a simple two-bus system and a fully-electrified active distribution network (ADN). Both case studies demonstrate the successful operation of grid-forming controlled PV systems, highlighting their capability to influence power system frequency dynamics. The analysis underscores the significance of deloading PV operation in facilitating flexibility services provision, thereby enhancing the reliability and resilience of system operation.

articleTitle: Insights into Household Energy Consumption: Disaggregating Cooling and Heating Profiles using Principal Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper develops a methodology based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to disaggregate distinct baseline electricity, heating and cooling components from the daily total electricity consumption data of 68 houses in Cyprus over the course of one year. The results show that the electricity data involves several principal components, with the two main ones accounting for 52.27% and 14.83% of the total variance, representing cooling and heating, respectively. The findings highlight the potential of using PCA for effective energy disaggregation, which could be extended to various building types and communities. By analyzing energy consumption patterns, targeted energy-saving and improved energy efficiency measures can be identified. Future research will compare PCA results with physics-driven building models, explore alternative disaggregation methods, and apply the methodology to broader datasets.

Index Terms: Sources Of Variation In The Data

articleTitle: Technical Analysis and Strategic Solutions for Aerial Fiber Optic Network Deployment in Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper explores critical technical factors in deploying aerial fiber optic networks, focusing on proximity to low and medium voltage overhead conductors, public lighting fixtures, ground clearance in various settings, and horizontal separation from buildings. The study reviews global standards, including insulated fiber optic technologies such as Kevlar and ADSS self-supporting cables, comparing them with Greek regulations. Proposed solutions address these technical challenges, offering tailored recommendations for optimal installations that meet regulatory requirements. The findings contribute to best practices in aerial fiber optic installations for both national and international contexts.

Author Keywords: Safety distances for power and IT cabling

articleTitle: Online Electromechanical Mode Identification from Power System Ringdown Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive methodology for the online identification of electromechanical modes. Within the proposed framework, a series of tasks is executed prior to mode estimation in order to efficiently handle ringdown data. These tasks include detecting the onset of a disturbance, extracting the optimum length of the ringdown, and further pre-processing the signal for enhanced analysis. To perform mode identification the Hybrid frequency/time-domain approach is used. The performance of the proposed methodology is tested using a synthetic signal which is intentionally distorted with noise and contains non-typical data. Results indicate the applicability and efficiency of the proposed method for the online identification of power systems electromechanical modes.

articleTitle: Study on the Development of an Underground Fiber Optic Network Alongside Electrical Distribution Systems in Greece
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This study explores the strategic integration of a fiber optic network within the existing underground electrical distribution infrastructure in Greece, facilitated by HEDNO. It aims to enhance the telecommunications framework while maintaining harmony with the electrical systems, contributing to sustainable infrastructure goals. The research assesses international standards such as ELOT EN 50174.03 and IEEE2023 National Electrical Safety Code, along with Greek regulations, to develop an installation plan that minimizes risks like electrical interference and environmental impacts. The analysis includes determining optimal burial depths, implementing protective measures, and maintaining safe distances between fiber optic and power cables. The paper provides visual representations of the installation methods, emphasizing the practical implementation of these guidelines. This study offers insights that could guide similar integrations worldwide, promoting technological progress alongside sustainable infrastructure development.

articleTitle: The Potential of Agrivoltaics' in the Iberian Peninsula: Analysis of three different crops
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The spread of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) installations raises concerns about land occupation by power plants hindering other land uses, like agriculture. The dual land use for agriculture and energy production, proposed by agrivoltaics can contribute to solving this problem. This study analyses the potential of potato, tomato, and lettuce crops areas for electricity production in Portugal and Spain. The viability of using these crops for agrivoltaics was inspected by determining the land equivalent ratio (LER). A LER higher than 1.0 was obtained for the three crops, proving their suitability for agrivoltaics applications. The contribution of agrivoltaics systems installed in these crops’ areas to the Portuguese and Spanish electricity demand and the respective 2030 PV capacity goals was estimated. It was concluded that using 20% of the potato crops’ area for agrivoltaics, could assure 7.5% and 6.2% of respectively Portugal’s and Spain’s electricity needs and cover 1.2% of the PV capacity goals for both countries.

articleTitle: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Electricity Costs in Building Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: In recent years, the world has shifted its focus towards sustainable energy sources. Efficient usage of renewable sources in buildings requires optimal usage of the fluctuating generation and battery systems. Reinforcement learning (RL) could play a key role in this optimization but mostly remains a black-box in previous applications. In this paper, we propose an Explainable RL (XRL) agent to solve the dynamic problem of cost optimization in energy systems and make it transparent by applying Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques. We demonstrate how the agent learns efficient policies, such as purchasing power at lower prices and selling it at high prices.

articleTitle: Synthetic Data for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring: A Markov Chain Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper deals with the generation of synthetic data, which plays an important role in the Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) problem. We introduce the NILM problem and then explain its crucial role in improving energy efficiency and supporting smart grid functions. The paper explains the stages of the NILM problem, including data acquisition, feature extraction, event detection, and appliance classification. We also explain two methods for generating synthetic data: AMBAL (Appliance Model Based Algorithm for Load monitoring) and SmartSim. Then, we propose a synthetic data generation method based on Markov chains, which is designed to generate labeled data useful for training supervised machine learning models. The proposed method utilizes the probabilistic transitions between different operational states of appliances, and captures the stochastic nature of real-world appliance usage. Thus, the generated synthetic data not only reflects realistic usage patterns, but also contains labels indicating the state of each appliance at a given time. The simulations are then run by generating synthetic data for typical office equipment such as laptops and televisions. The generated data sets provide detailed and accurate usage profiles, which are important for the effective training and validation of NILM algorithms. Since the generated data also includes the labeled data, this method will improve the ability of NILM systems to accurately identify and monitor individual appliances in a complex load environment.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Low Frequency Characteristics of Li-ion Cells using Laplace Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Lithium Ion (Li-ion) cells are efficient energy storage devices with high energy density and long life, but their performance changes over time due to aging mechanisms sensitive to conditions like temperature, current, and state-of-charge range. Each cell ages uniquely, requiring methods to identify the underlying causes. This work presents an automated approach to assess changes in diffusive resistance from voltage relaxation curves. Using finite length Warburg elements, Laplace inversion, and particle swarm optimization, diffusion modelling elements are fit to time domain data. The approach was demonstrated using a 9-month ageing study of Nickel-Manganese-Cobalt/Gr cells at 45°C. Analysis results show early life and gradual increase in late life. Diffusion resistances showed localized trends due to the movement of electrode phase changes relative to cell state-of-charge. Diffusion time constants elongate consistently over life. This shows control systems must adapt for complex resistance parameter changes and significant dynamic effects during lifetime.

articleTitle: Modelling Building-Integrated Photovoltaic/Thermal Systems: Sensitivity Analysis Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Transformation of buildings to solar-powered structures can support the evolution of the global energy network towards a decentralized and environmentally sustainable system. Building-integrated photovoltaics thermal (BIPV/T) systems can play a crucial role in this process by facilitating the decarbonization of the heating sector through electrification. By generating both electrical and thermal energy from the same surface area their overall efficiency is improved making them particularly advantageous in dense urban environments where space is limited. The main design parameters which influence the BIPV/T energy performance include geometric features of the system such as channel length and height, inclination, and orientation as well as control parameters such as the air flow rate that runs through the BIPV/T channel.In this study a sensitivity analysis on selected design parameters of a BIPV/T system coupled to an air-source heat pump is conducted to identify sensitive features that have the biggest impact on the system performance.Key findings include that longer BIPV/T channels heighten the importance of channel height in the thermal production of the BIPV/T system, while higher channel air velocities generally decrease the impact of geometric parameters. Finally, the analysis indicated that there is a critical range of channel heights and lengths within which the sensitivity of these parameters on the outlet temperature of the BIPV/T channel is maximized.

articleTitle: Handling of Computationally Demanding Digital Controllers in Power System Dynamic Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Nowadays Smart grids utilize digital controllers to guarantee the reliable and efficient operation of their components. However, the numerical simulation of these types of controllers is challenging due to the numerous discrete time events introduced. The interpolation-based method (IBM) can effectively simulate smart digital controllers alongside the differential-algebraic equations of the system under control. Compared to the traditional step-reduction method (SRM) that reduces the time step for each time event during the simulation, IBM allows the use of variable time steps and solves the system while ensuring simulation accuracy. However, in the case of computationally demanding controllers, the computational performance of IBM suffers significantly. In this paper, a modified version of IBM is introduced, which can handle computationally demanding controllers in dynamic simulation of power systems. The performance of the proposed method is assessed and compared to SRM and IBM by simulating a test system with different controllers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Efficiency in Mediterranean Residential Buildings: The Role of Double Façades and Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This study investigates the potential of double façade systems integrated with photovoltaic technology to enhance the energy efficiency of residential buildings in Mediterranean climates. Using a one-bedroom studio module in Nicosia, Cyprus, various configurations of conventional double façades, building-integrated photovoltaics, and photovoltaic thermal systems were analyzed. The study simulated thermal loads and primary energy consumption using EnergyPlus and DesignBuilder, examining different cavity depths to optimize performance. Results indicate that BIPV/T systems significantly reduce both heating and cooling loads, achieving the best overall energy performance. The optimal cavity depth of 0.97 m not only minimized energy consumption but also provided additional usable space. These findings underscore the importance of integrating renewable energy technologies in urban planning to meet nearly zero energy building standards.

articleTitle: Comparing Sweep Rate Effects for Different Perovskite Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Perovskite solar cell devices – although thought to be possible candidates for substituting conventional silicon photovoltaics – display inherent instabilities that complicate the application of traditional characterisation approaches. Hence, conducting measurements for different technologies under varying conditions can help in characterising them as well as contributing to the advancement of their stability needed for commercial success. This work aims to contribute to the growing body of indoor tests aimed at enhancing the understanding and characterisation of this novel technology. Four different types of perovskite technology mini-modules have been tested with different sweep rates to study its impact on the hysteresis effect noticed during full scan current-voltage (I-V) traces. Measurements revealed that the MAPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite-based devices are more sensitive to sweep rate than the CsFAPbIBr perovskites. The changes noticed in the I-V traces at different sweep rates is thought to be due to different ion migration effects in the perovskite, so finding the appropriate sweep rate for each technology will lead to a better characterisation of these samples.

articleTitle: Towards edge-computed NILM: Insights from a Mediterranean Use Case
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: An optimized structured pruning methodology within the context of Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is introduced. The proposed methodology exploits unstructured pruning to determine the optimal sparsity ratio for each layer in the deep neural network model. Subsequently, structured pruning is applied to remove entire units from each layer according to the sparsity values guided by the unstructured pruning. By doing so, important feature information is preserved, resulting in improved classification performance as the pruning threshold is not arbitrarily selected based on a random percentage ratio. Experimental results, evaluated on the Plegma dataset—one of the first datasets from the Mediterranean area capturing local devices and consumption patterns—demonstrate that the proposed methodology significantly optimizes inference performance. Specifically, the approach reduces the baseline model’s MFLOPs by up to 48.85% while keeping a satisfactory disaggregation performance, a stark contrast to the widely used unstructured pruning approach, which does not achieve FLOPs reduction. These findings underscore the potential of edge NILM for promoting flexibility and energy transition in the Mediterranean region, facilitating the broader adoption and implementation of NILM solutions in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Techno-economic evaluation of Energy Community configurations based on the individual economic benefit of the members: the case of Cyprus
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) enable the participation of citizens in the energy transition, facilitating the shift towards a consumer-centric energy system. Given the voluntary and open nature of ECs, the participation of citizens can be challenging, especially in the early stages of development. This paper addresses this by evaluating the individual economic benefits of existing or potential EC members under different EC configurations. Three basic EC configurations were examined for the case of Cyprus: (i) the EC acting as an electricity producer and exporter, (ii) the EC acting as an electricity producer for maximum self-consumption, and (iii) the EC members trading energy among themselves using an EC-based local electricity market. The results showcased the potential of ECs as an alternative to traditional RES residential schemes, while also highlighting the economic challenges associated with implementing such configurations.

articleTitle: Introduction of hydrogen technologies to mitigate the impact of thermal consumption in a university campus
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: It is imperative for energy systems to reduce their environmental footprint in a cost-efficient manner, for which renwable energy sources (RES) and complementary technologies become desirable options to achieve said task. This is particularly the case for systems with different energy sources, as they’d be able to either address one specific type of energy demand and/or allow for the coupling of different energy carriers that would allow for technologies that normally don’t interact to start complementing each other. Therefore, this paper proposes various scenarios for the UCY campus in which hydrogen technologies would allow for the electrification of thermal demand while harnessing the surplus production coming from a solar park, which is modelled through the Integrate optimization tool and validated through DidSILENT PowerFactory. The results showcased a rise of up to 58% in self-sufficiency while the annual energy costs and CO2 emissions were reduced by 45% and 48% respectively.

articleTitle: Examining the economic feasibility of hybrid Photovoltaic – Battery Energy Storage System in public building with flexible demand: Cyprus case study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Photovoltaic – Battery Energy Storage Systems (PVBESS) are a promising solution against technical bottlenecks of high PV penetration. Public buildings are suitable for installation, although currently underexploited, while high BESS costs limit technology diffusion. This paper assesses the economic feasibility of PV-BESS in public buildings with flexible demand, through simulations showcasing BESS subsidisation impact and self-sufficiency contribution. The results derived that smaller PV-BESS sizes are more attractive investments, as larger systems are characterised by reduced profitability, while BESS subsidisation enhances system profitability. Shifting a small portion of load demand improves economic feasibility by decreasing BESS size, while combining PV production, energy storage, and energy flexibility is the optimal solution for public buildings against electricity prices. Finally, a trade-off between economic feasibility and energy self-sufficiency is observed. The results can be utilised by policymakers to design strategies for BESS promotion, while professionals can perform accurate system sizing, thus avoiding excess system capacities.

articleTitle: Enhancing user comfort in smart buildings though operational optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper presents a multi- objective operational model for smart buildings, integrating Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems, electrical storage, Light-Emitting Diode (LED) lighting, and photovoltaic (PV) devices. The model addresses the challenges of HVAC system non-linearity, optimizing both economic efficiency and occupant comfort. Designed for scalability and real-time applications, the model minimizes energy costs while ensuring thermal comfort, optimal lighting, and maintaining air quality within healthy CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> levels. Additionally, the study includes a Pareto frontier, offering a range of optimal solutions that balance energy savings with comfort requirements. This approach enhances both cost-effectiveness and occupant well-being in smart buildings, providing decision-makers with flexibility in prioritizing between economic and comfort objectives.

articleTitle: Flexibility within market coupling in Southeast Europe
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This work addresses the problem of optimizing the energy market-clearing of an integrated power system in a coupled market. More specifically, a wide range of market products (simple hourly, block, and complex orders) are simulated in order to determine the optimal energy allocation. Apart from conventional power plants, a series of flexibility service providers are also modeled, including electricity storage systems and electric vehicles under various smart charging and discharging options. The overall methodological framework is based on mixed-integer programming techniques and is tested in the integrated Greek-Bulgarian-Romanian power system as planned for 2030. A series of scenarios have also been examined to investigate the impacts of parameters such as PV availability, electricity demand, EV penetration, and natural gas and CO2 emission prices. The results highlight the impacts of market coupling in a series of fundamentals such as resulting energy mix, cross-border electricity flows, and environmental impact in terms of CO2 emissions. It also underscores the role of flexible resources in alleviating the impacts of intermittency injected into the power systems through variable renewable energy sources. System operators, regulatory authorities, and potential investors can utilize the optimization framework developed to quantify the short-term dynamics of coupled electricity market operations and optimize the management of their resources and portfolios.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Smart Readiness Indicator Scheme: Methodology Assessment through 20 Use Cases
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The European Union developed the Smart Readiness Indicator (SRI) to enhance energy efficiency and encourage the adoption of smart technologies in buildings, tackling their high energy usage and carbon emissions. This study evaluates the SRI methodology through the assessment of 20 diverse use cases, including residential and non-residential buildings, using Methods A and B of the SRI assessment scheme. Key variables such as climate zone, building type, year of construction, and the integration of smart-ready services were considered to ensure a comprehensive evaluation.Five engineers assessed the buildings using the SRI EU Excel Tool and rated the methodology based on criteria including accuracy, usability, comprehensiveness, flexibility, and impact on decision-making. The results revealed high ratings for accuracy (45% rated as "Very Good" and 30% as "Excellent") and usability (50% rated as "Very Good"), while comprehensiveness was rated more moderately (40% "Good"). However, flexibility and adaptability emerged as areas requiring improvement, with 45% of assessments rated as "Fair." The SRI methodology demonstrated strong potential but requires further refinement to address the needs of diverse building types and more complex smart technologies. The study concludes that the SRI framework is a valuable tool for promoting energy efficiency and smart technology adoption across the EU building sector. However, additional research is recommended to integrate real-time data and automation technologies, and to enhance the framework's scalability and adaptability for future building systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Residential Net Load using Demand Response and Battery Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Demand side management (DSM) and solar-plus-storage systems are enabling technologies that facilitate consumers to increase self-consumption (SC), while reducing electricity costs through efficient and intelligent electricity usage. Even though many demand response (DR) strategies have been presented for the residential sector, a major challenge remains the joint optimal utilization and synergies of DR and the battery systems flexibility scheduling. This paper explores how the optimization of DR and battery energy storage systems (BESS) scheduling can notably improve the net load profile of residential users. The obtained results indicate that the optimized DR model and battery storage effectively support load shifting and peak energy utilization. Specifically, the analysis suggests that the combination of DR and an 8kWh battery storage system increased the SC from 55.04% to 95.84% and the SS from 37.50% to 66.88%, compared to a baseline scenario (without battery storage and DR actions).
