Ultimately, the proposed optimization achieved a higher degree of energy autonomy for the yearly profile of a median household by minimizing the sum of absolute values of the net load with load shifting and BESS charging/discharging. Finally, the optimization model can be used by aggregators and system operators for scheduling and optimizing flexibility actions.

articleTitle: Floating Photovoltaics in Spain: Analysis of the Sierra Brava Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Increasing photovoltaic energy production is one of the most cost-effective strategies to reduce energy associated CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. As such, global deployment of photovoltaic (PV) systems has been growing firmly. Installing PV systems on water surfaces (floating PV or FPV) is a promising solution to sustain such growth, as it utilizes water surfaces to produce energy. Here, we present an analysis of the energy production of the FPV plant in Sierra Brava, Spain. The plant uses different floating PV technologies, as well as distinct azimuthal orientations and inclinations. Using the software PVSyst, the energy production of the two different fields of the power plant is estimated and compared with the actual production data, for the period between February 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and February 27<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 2022. The energy production gain from placing the PV system on water instead of land was also estimated. It was observed that for the FPV configurations analyzed, there was a good agreement between the simulated and measured results, thus validating the model.

articleTitle: Propagating the uncertainties of the overhead line span vulnerability model up to the failure return period in case of extreme events
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The operation of electric power systems may be affected by the failure of system components due to adverse weather events. Consequently, the assessment of the "resilience" property, meant as the ability to limit the extent, severity, and duration of system degradation due to such disruptive events, becomes a fundamental task. In resilience analyses, uncertainty sources should be properly represented and quantified. This work proposes an approach based on the Point Estimation Method (PEM) to assess the probability distributions of the failure return periods of overhead line spans, starting from the uncertainties in the span vulnerability model. The approach is applied to three transmission lines exposed to wind loads. Results show that PEM is suitable for uncertainty propagation in the resilience assessment methodology. In particular, different behaviors of the spans are highlighted, in terms of uncertainty of their failure probabilities.

articleTitle: Synergy between biogas and concentrating solar thermal - case study of a dairy industry in Cyprus
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The present study investigates the potential incorporation of a Linear Fresnel Reflector to directly supply heat for the processes of a local dairy industry, namely, Petrou Bros Dairy Products, located in the outskirts of Larnaca, Cyprus. The company already possesses an infrastructure of biogas generation based on organic waste that arises from its own cheese production. The biogas is used in a dual-fuel boiler which delivers steam for milk pasteurization and cheese cooking. The daily profile includes two intervals when biogas is unavailable, and light fuel oil is used instead. The latter is a fossil fuel with high carbon intensity, hence, the present study elaborates its substitution with solar thermal energy, and therefore enhance the sustainability, as well as the circularity of the process. A transient, year-long OpenModelica model is employed for the simulation of five solar field size scenarios.

articleTitle: Attaining reactive power capability requirements for offshore wind power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The prospected diffusion of offshore wind farms (OWFs), to be connected to high-voltage transmission networks, arises the need of dealing with specific technical requirements posed in grid codes by transmission system operators (TSOs). Among them, the compliance with specific reactive power capabilities at point of common coupling can have significant implications in the design stage, for the definition of the needed size and position of compensation devices. In this context, an optimisation problem is proposed in this paper to determine the size of a reactive power compensation device coping with grid code requirements to connect an OWF to transmission system. The problem involves full AC load flow constraints along with nodal voltage and power rating boundaries. The proposed procedure is applied to an offshore wind farm test system to attain the Italian TSO grid code rules.

articleTitle: A framework for evaluating contributions of Inverter Based Resources to grid performance
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The drive towards fully decarbonized power systems leads to the widespread replacement of synchronous generators (SG) by Inverter Based Resources (IBR) which should replace not just the energy, but also the services SGs supplied to the system. Inverters interfacing renewables to grids have considerable control flexibility but also certain limitations compared to SG that arise from the nature of power electronics and the resource. Different inverter control configurations can bring distinct system benefits and supply services in new ways. The framework proposed in this paper seeks to join the two sides of the debate on services in future power systems - what can inverters do and what does the system need - and thereby ease the uptake of inverters with grid-supporting capabilities. An evaluation procedure is proposed to quantify the value an inverter installation adds to the system by providing a range of services. A metrics set is defined across three categories, namely, Inverter Metrics, IBR Features and Network Metrics. Inverter Metrics, which are influenced by IBR Features, quantify the inverter’s services provision capacity. These are weighted based on the locational system’s needs for each service as judged by the Network Metrics. The all-round value an inverter adds to the system is calculated from a weighted sum of each service score and indicates not only the inverter’s capacity to provide services but also the importance of their provision for the system. It is intended that this framework could form the basis of an incentives scheme for services provision by IBR.

articleTitle: Leveraging Ancillary Services from Building Thermostatic Loads in Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The integration of large-scale renewable energy sources and the incorporation of state-of-the-art technologies in contemporary power systems require advanced control techniques to maintain the stability of the power grids. One solution could be building thermostatic loads to provide ancillary services like operating reserves. The possibility of using buildings' thermostatic loads to contribute to grid services is facilitated by automatic generation control (AGC), which is thoroughly discussed in this paper. The building thermostatic load (BTL) can be flexibly controlled to provide the grid signal with an automatic short-term reserve capacity. To utilize the reserve provisioning capability of BTLs, a comprehensive power grid model with an AGC system is developed using the DIgSilent power factory software. The model integrates different power plants, including wind energy generation stations, thermal power stations, gas-fired power stations, and BTLs. A dynamic power allocation strategy is developed for the proposed power model and implemented using 12-hour simulations. The analysis results revealed that integration of BTLs into the power grid assists in balanced demand and supply of power systems and also enhances the efficiencies and reliability of the power system network.

articleTitle: User-Focused Evaluation of Hydrogen Integration for a Gas Distribution Network in Southern Italy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The European Union is reducing its dependencies on fossil fuels, including natural gas, to meet decarbonisation objectives for 2050. However, in 2023, Natural Gas accounted for 17% of the energy source and an extensive infrastructure supporting it. This reason is pushing researchers towards numerous studies in natural gas blending with green fuels from renewable sources including biogas or green hydrogen. Despite ongoing research, it is necessary to investigate the impact of the hydrogen injection into the network from a user perspective, as the lower heat value of the resulting mixture will inevitably be reduced with the addition of low calorific fuel like hydrogen. For this purpose, this study evaluates the potential feasibility of hydrogen introduction into a real network from an Italian case study, focusing on lower heat value analysis, gas interchangeability and user consumption. After evaluating gas quality parameters such as Wobbe Index, specific gravity and Higher Heating Value it was possible to estimate the maximum value of blending hydrogen into the distribution of a ring-topology network to be 13.50 % and its impact on CO2 reduction.

articleTitle: Integrating Photovoltaics and Battery Energy Storage Systems under Corporate Power Purchase Agreements and Market Exposure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic with Battery Energy Storage Systems under corporate Power Purchase Agreements presents opportunities for renewable energy producers to enhance their financial and operational performance. This paper investigates the economic viability and strategic benefits of such integration, emphasizing the importance of optimal Battery Energy Storage Systems sizing and advanced market participation strategies. By employing probabilistic Bayesian Long Short-Term Memory network for long-term photovoltaic power output forecasting, we enable the Renewable Energy Producer to manage risk and secure stable power supply contracts. Our analysis demonstrates that maximum profitability is achieved with a safety level of z = 2 and battery duration of two hours, with annual profit of 1.08 million euros in non-congested market conditions. In congested markets, the strategy proves resilient, maintaining substantial profitability. The study underscores the critical role of accurate forecasting, robust market analysis, and strategic decision-making in optimizing the financial outcomes of co-located installations.

Author Keywords: co-location photovoltaic and battery energy storage systems

articleTitle: Advancing Energy Communities in Southeastern Europe: The SunSharing Project
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) are promoted by European Union to play a key role in achieving the goal of a just energy transition with active participation of citizens. Many countries are adopting relevant European Directives and integrate ECs in their legislative framework. To this direction, this paper concentrates on analyzing the existing conditions around the establishment and the operation of ECs in southeastern European countries, mainly focusing on Croatia, Greece, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria. Although there is high potential for utilizing energy from renewable sources, especially solar energy, in these countries, the lack of adequate legislation on ECs and the lack of crowdfunding initiatives hinders the penetration of community-based photovoltaic systems. In the context of SunSharing project, funded by the European Climate Initiative (EUKI), in which these countries participate as partners, this study aims to provide good practice examples for ECs and crowdfunding initiatives that could inspire the further development of ECs and related energy projects.

articleTitle: Green hydrogen integration in the built environment: Cost-risk analysis via stochastic optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Green hydrogen offers a long-term energy storage solution for excess renewable electricity, which can enhance building self-sufficiency and energy resilience. However, electrolysers and fuel cells involve high investment costs. In this work, a stochastic optimisation framework is developed which incorporates uncertainty into an energy planning tool performing technology design and operation optimisation. The potential of green hydrogen when coupled to electricity, heating and cooling systems is investigated for a hypothetical household community in the Mediterranean region, addressing the fundamental question: How does accounting for the impact of uncertainties associated with future electricity prices affect the economic viability of green hydrogen in residential communities? The results show that a risk-prone strategy lowers expected costs by 8%, but a risk-averse approach reduces risk by 5%. Overall, considering uncertainty in the optimisation problem strengthens the role of green hydrogen in risk-averse strategies, requiring higher investments but reducing dependence on future resource price fluctuations.

articleTitle: The CONCERTI Project: from Magliano Alpi’s Energy Community to an Innovative Integrated Inter-Municipal Energy Sharing Paradigm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Energy communities, envisioned by the European regulatory framework, are innovative forms of production, consumption and sharing of locally produced renewable energy. Italy began its development of renewable energy communities in 2019, with experimental transitional legislation, and only in early 2024 did the overall framework settle down. As the regulatory framework has evolved, energy communities have taken on different potentials than originally envisioned, both in terms of economics and spatial extent. In this continually evolving context, the CONCERTI project, an ambitious initiative aimed at enhancing the concept of energy communities at the market area level, highlights the shift in the integration of energy communities into a more extended territorial system, toward new frontiers of distributed production and consumption, including with the introduction of aggregating entities capable of having members of energy communities participate in electricity and service markets.

articleTitle: Net Load Prediction Using Machine Learning Methods: A Case Study of Residential Households
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: As residential solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are increasingly integrated into distribution networks globally, there is a growing necessity to shift from traditional load forecasting to net load forecasting (i.e., predicting the combination of PV and load collectively). Understanding and predicting the daily net energy of a typical household is crucial for designing and sizing appropriate renewable energy systems and storage solutions. This paper compares the performance of different machine learning methods in predicting the net load patterns of a typical household. The database contained PV production and energy load records from 68 actual households in Cyprus, over a period of one year. The results showed that the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model outperformed all other models yielding a normalized root mean square error of 5.52%. Despite the inherent unpredictability of net load patterns, the findings indicate that the proposed XGBoost model can achieve high prediction accuracies for household electricity net load profiles.

articleTitle: The Greek Balancing Market: an overview of current and future mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The Greek Balancing Market is crucial in sustaining the balance between electricity supply and demand within the Hellenic Electricity Transmission System (HETS). Under the governance of the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO) and utilizing a central dispatch/unit-based model, this market operates through the Balancing Capacity Market, Balancing Energy Market, and Imbalance Settlement mechanisms. This paper offers a comprehensive analysis of the Greek Balancing Market, detailing the roles of market participants, the Integrated Scheduling Process (ISP), and real-time balancing operations. The effectiveness, challenges, and future prospects of the market are examined, highlighting its role in ensuring system stability, fostering competition, and promoting transparency and efficiency in Greece's electricity sector.

articleTitle: Optimal coordination of a pool of different EV charging stations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: The transport sector will contribute to the decarbonisation goals by massively replacing internal combustion engine vehicles with electric vehicles (EVs). In Europe, up to 70 million EVs are expected by 2030. The diffusion of EVs will be accompanied by 50-70 million charging points connected to the distribution systems (at medium and low voltage levels). The EV charging causes power quality and operation issues, such as line overloading, voltage violations, and voltage unbalances. It will require extensive investments to develop a distribution system suited to face the electrification of heating and transportation. Using suitable control systems for optimal charging that consider charging session features and network criticalities can mitigate the impact of EVs on distribution grids and contribute to postponing or even avoiding significant investments. The paper proposes a strategy to reduce the effects of public charging on low-voltage networks. If already burdened by the increased electrification of end-use consumption and domestic vehicle charging, these networks are susceptible to significant voltage drops or overcurrents. The proposed strategy involves developing a signalling system that informs vehicle owners whether a charging station can guarantee a full charge based on current grid conditions. An Italian LV unbalanced network and charging habits in parking lots derived from the latest literature are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Green hydrogen storage capacity estimations in depleted gas reservoirs
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Green hydrogen is poised to play a crucial role in the transition to renewable energy sources. It acts as a versatile energy storage carrier, helping to balance supply and demand. However, storing hydrogen presents significant challenges, as current technologies can only handle limited volumes. One promising solution involves injecting hydrogen into depleted oil & gas reservoirs, where it can be stored and later extracted when needed. This study explores this approach using the material balance method, which estimates the volumes within a reservoir. It is applied to a depleted natural gas system supported by an aquifer, taking into account pressure and flow rate histories. As the natural gas production rate increases, the hydrogen storage capacity also rises preventing the water to invade in the reservoir. For example, at a reference pressure of 2000 psi, there is no hydrogen storage capacity at a flow rate of 10 MMMCF/day, whereas a storage capacity of 314 BSCF is observed at a flow rate of 1000 MMMCF/day. These insights highlight the potential of utilising depleted reservoirs for hydrogen storage, offering a feasible path to overcoming the current limitations in hydrogen storage technology.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning based Energy Management System for Controlling Storage Systems in a Cluster of Buildings: Cypriot use case
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: In this paper, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) energy management system is developed to control various energy storage systems such as a cooling storage system, domestic hot water (DHW) storage tank, and also electrical storage systems (batteries) to increase the share of solar energy consisting of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and solar collectors. The main aim is to study a cluster of three buildings in Cyprus, to enhance the energy flexibility and efficiency in both demand and supply sides. To this end, the collected measured data is preprocessed and utilized in CityLearn, a data-driven simulation environment, to train a DRL controller for managing distributed energy systems. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is applied to evaluate the indoor dynamic temperature in each building, and then the developed DRL algorithm coordinates energy systems across the buildings. The results are compared with an optimized Rule-Based Controller (RBC) to demonstrate reductions according to proposed key performance indicators (KPIs): Average Daily Peak, Thermal Resilience Index, and Zero Net Energy. The results show that the proposed approach in this cluster of buildings significantly reduces the demand by up to 29%, especially during peak hours by consuming renewable energy sources (RES), and improves the overall performance of the building energy system.

articleTitle: EnTRAINER’s Project Tools Framework for Energy Transition Audits Towards Decarbonization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper presents the tools framework that were developed in the context of the EnTRAINER LIFE21 CET project. The tools that comprise the framework were built to allow energy managers and energy experts of industries to assess the energy and CO2 saving potentials but also to aid during the energy transition audits that will occur during the project. The framework is composed of four tools. The first tool utilizes the cumulative sum (CUSUM) methodology to detect consumption anomalies or extreme deviations from the baseline pattern of the company’s consumption. The second tool offers a quantified estimation of the building’s insulation status, while the third one is composed of four simple questions that can detect energy efficiency potentials in the involved site. Finally, the fourth tool aims to create part of the energy transition audit report that will occur in the project.

articleTitle: Exploring Energy Culture and Efficiency Awareness: Insights from Private and Public Sectors in Romania
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper focuses on the energy transition as a social transition and highlights the importance of understanding individual and collective behaviors, aspirations and perceptions regarding energy consumption. The conceptual framework of energy cultures serves as a basic tool for investigating energy behavior, facilitating a deeper understanding of the factors influencing energy consumption. The study, carried out within the ENERGEIA project, focuses on assessing energy culture and energy efficiency awareness in both private entities and public institutions in Romania. Using a comprehensive questionnaire tool, the research aims to uncover the main challenges and barriers faced by organizations in implementing energy efficiency measures. The paper presents a quantitative analysis of the survey data aiming to gather information about the energy culture of companies and public bodies to identify common opportunities for action to improve energy culture and awareness levels.

articleTitle: Large scale hydrogen production technologies – review and case study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: High energy prices and climate change have increased interest in hydrogen production, storage, and usage. Hydrogen is an energy vector that promises many opportunities for the electricity, natural gas sectors, transportation, and various other industries. The article highlights the importance and interest in hydrogen production in past years and focuses on the main large-scale methods of producing hydrogen. This article presents a case study with two hydrogen production methods, presenting the financial point of view considering actual prices. In the end, a table summarizes all the methods of hydrogen production highlighting the advantages and disadvantages of each one, the overall efficiency, and finally, the cost of hydrogen production was also included.

articleTitle: Aligning EV Education with Industry Needs in Southeast Europe
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: As European car manufacturers increasingly commit to fully electric vehicles in alignment with the European Green Deal and EU climate targets, the transition from internal combustion engines to electric vehicles necessitates a new skill set for engineers, particularly in Southeastern Europe. This paper examines the integration of industry feedback in developing an EV-focused curriculum across four Southeastern European countries. The EvolvEV project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme, aims to support climate action by creating an open-access learning platform to advance technical and entrepreneurial skills in the EV sector. It addresses the skill gaps by developing specialized courses aligned with industry needs, promoting practical knowledge, and fostering continuous collaboration between academia and industry. Key technical and non-technical skills required by the EV industry are identified through stakeholder consultations, highlighting the need for updated educational programs that balance theoretical knowledge with practical application and non-technical competencies.

articleTitle: Strategies for Optimizing Energy Efficiency in Residential Buildings: An Integrated Framework Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: Sustainable design and nearly zero-energy buildings (NZEBs) are essential for managing energy consumption and reducing carbon emissions in the building sector while maintaining occupant comfort. This study focuses on developing an advanced modeling framework for optimizing energy efficiency in residential buildings, integrating computational design, building performance simulation, and multi-objective optimization (MOO). Applied to a typical archetype in Cyprus, the framework evaluates diverse energy-efficient strategies, including innovative measures such as thermochromic glazing, natural ventilation, automated dimming of artificial lighting, and rule-based control electrochromic glazing systems, among other conventional energy efficiency measures (EEMs). MOO considers energy needs and investment costs. Results demonstrate significant energy savings potential, with optimal combinations of EEMs achieving a 77% reduction in cooling demand and 73% in heating demand compared to the baseline. This tool proves valuable for decision-making in both new construction and retrofitting, identifying cost-effective pathways towards NZEBs.

articleTitle: Towards dynamic pricing algorithm for residential buildings: A Model Predictive Control framework for load aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: With the rise of aggregators, establishing an effective pricing framework for electricity allocation among substations serving residential customers is crucial. This paper proposes a method for large-scale demand-side flexibility, smart thermostat data, along with ambient temperature and heating power measurements, are utilized to calibrate models of reduced-order resistance-capacitance (RC) thermal networks for buildings. A Monte Carlo framework evaluates the optimal level of demand-side management (DSM), strategy diversification, and uncertainty in aggregated demand, guiding an economic Model Predictive Control framework for day-ahead coordination market. Simulations conducted on numerous homes in Toronto, Ontario, demonstrate that implementing medium-to-high DSM can enhance grid stability, leading to a 94% increase in load factor. The findings suggest that a balanced portfolio of aggregation provides the most benefit, and a three-tier tariff structure results more effective for load flattening than a two-tier system. This approach offers a viable pathway to improve electricity grid management in residential areas.

articleTitle: Energy modeling of integrated photovoltaic-thermal panels with thermoelectric systems in buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel building-integrated solar system combining Photovoltaic/Thermal (PV/T) panels and thermoelectric coolers (TEC). The PV/T panels increase electricity efficiency by cooling the PV cells, simultaneously generating electricity and thermal energy. TEC devices provide space cooling or heating through heat transfer controlled by the direction of the electrical current. By integrating PV/T panels with TEC devices, various PVT-TEC system layouts can be created to meet a building's electricity, heating, and cooling demands while enhancing the self-consumption rate of PV production. To evaluate the energy performance of PVT-TEC systems, a new 2D dynamic simulation model using a resistive-capacitance thermal network was developed. This model is implemented in a MATLAB-based tool to analyze building energy performance. The tool allows for comparing different PVT-TEC configurations from both energy and economic perspectives.

articleTitle: Classifying Tomorrow’s Currents: A Probabilistic Neural Network Approach to Forecasting Electricity Prices
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This study introduces a probabilistic neural network model for classifying next-day electricity prices into negative or positive categories. It addresses the challenge of price volatility exacerbated by renewable energy integration, presenting significant risks for market participants. Through a comparative analysis with the traditional support vector machine with radial basis function kernel using the German Day-Ahead market data of 2020, the probabilistic neural network demonstrates superior accuracy and yielded promising electricity price forecasting results. This approach equips market participants with valuable insights for strategic planning and risk mitigation.

articleTitle: Planning deep integration of energy communities in urban context: A GIS approach to optimise renewables, storage systems and demand aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Energy Transition in the Mediterranean Area (SyNERGY MED)
abstract: This paper addresses the critical need to reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and fossil fuel dependence by promoting renewable energy communities (RECs). A comprehensive methodology for planning, modelling, and evaluating RECs, with a focus on urban contexts, has been developed. The framework utilizes GIS for spatial analysis, urban building energy modelling, and a Monte Carlo method for aggregating RECs. Key steps include selecting district buildings, modelling energy consumption based on archetypal profiles, and assessing integration of renewable energy technologies and storage systems. The framework assesses different virtual building aggregations within the enabling framework of the renewable energy communities (RECs), optimising for self-consumption, self-sufficiency, and life cycle costs. Applied to a case study, the results indicate that urban areas benefit more from multiple smaller RECs rather than a few large ones, enhancing renewable energy usage and reducing life cycle costs. These findings highlight the potential for more efficient and sustainable energy solutions in urban environments through well-planned and optimized RECs.
